a.h1.text: Brief A: Freya Bank, early-stage collections, one product

a.p1.text: Freya Bank is fictional. Every customer, debt and payment here is synthetic.

a.p2.text: This brief has the density of a real bank specification. Read all of it. Most failed cases come from one rule that was skipped.

a.p3.text: Freya Bank calls customers who are 1 to 45 days late on one product. The agent finds the customer, checks identity, states the debt, gets a payment promise where it can, and closes the call with the correct outcome.

a.p4.text: Every call starts with these. Nothing else is known before the tools are called.

a.t1.r1.text: Variable: `customer_id`; Example: `c_4f2a...`; Meaning: Pass it to every tool call.

a.t1.r2.text: Variable: `first_name`, `last_name`; Example: `Daniel`, `Reyes`; Meaning: The person to ask for.

a.t1.r3.text: Variable: `title`; Example: `Mr` or `Ms`; Meaning: Address the customer as title plus last name.

a.t1.r4.text: Variable: `now`; Example: `2026-10-14T11:00`; Meaning: The current date and time. All date rules use this, never the real clock.

a.h4.text: 3. Opening and who is on the line

a.r1.text: First sentence: say you are a digital assistant calling from Freya Bank, and that the call is recorded. Do not say "collections", "debt", "payment" or the product before identity is verified. This applies to everyone, including relatives.

b.h1.text: Brief B: Freya Bank, up to three products

b.p1.text: Freya Bank is fictional. Every customer, debt and payment here is synthetic.

b.p2.text: Brief B is Brief A with a customer who can be late on up to three products. Every rule of Brief A applies unless a rule below replaces it.

b.r1.text: `get_account` returns one to three products. Each has its own `past_due`, `days_late` and floor.

b.r1.s2.text: Each has its own `past_due`, `days_late` and floor.

b.r2.text: State every late product, one sentence each, before asking for anything.

b.r3.text: The band and the deadline are per product, from that product's `days_late`. Two products of the same customer can have different deadlines.

b.r3.s1.text: The band and the deadline are per product, from that product's `days_late`.

b.r3.s2.text: Two products of the same customer can have different deadlines.

b.r4.text: First ask whether the customer can pay all of them today. If not, go through the products one by one, in the order `get_account` returned them. Do not ask about today again for each product. Start each product at attempt 1 of Brief A rule 30.

b.r4.s1.text: First ask whether the customer can pay all of them today.

b.r4.s2.text: If not, go through the products one by one, in the order `get_account` returned them.

b.r4.s3.text: Do not ask about today again for each product.

b.r4.s4.text: Start each product at attempt 1 of Brief A rule 30.

b.r5.text: Persuasion attempts are counted per product.

b.r6.text: If the customer names one date for everything and it is after one product's deadline, record that product on its own deadline and say so in the read-back. The other products keep the date the customer named.

b.r6.s1.text: If the customer names one date for everything and it is after one product's deadline, record that product on its own deadline and say so in the read-back.

b.r6.s2.text: The other products keep the date the customer named.

b.r7.text: Read all promises back together and ask for one confirmation. Then call `create_promise` once per product.

b.r7.s1.text: Read all promises back together and ask for one confirmation.

b.r8.text: The customer may promise some products and refuse others. For each product without a promise call `add_note` with that `product_id` and a reason: `refused`, `hardship`, `dispute`, `paid` or `service_error`. This also applies when no product gets a promise.

b.r8.s1.text: The customer may promise some products and refuse others.

b.r8.s2.text: For each product without a promise call `add_note` with that `product_id` and a reason: `refused`, `hardship`, `dispute`, `paid` or `service_error`.

b.r8.s3.text: This also applies when no product gets a promise.

b.r9.text: A dispute or an "already paid" claim on one product does not end the call. Note it and continue with the others.

b.r9.s1.text: A dispute or an "already paid" claim on one product does not end the call.

b.r9.s2.text: Note it and continue with the others.

b.r10.text: A restructuring request still transfers the call (Brief A rule 41). Promises recorded before the request stay. Promises agreed but not yet recorded are not recorded. Close as `transferred` / `restructuring`. On any transfer (restructuring, support, human) add no notes at all, before or after it.

b.r10.s3.text: Promises agreed but not yet recorded are not recorded.

b.r10.s5.text: On any transfer (restructuring, support, human) add no notes at all, before or after it.

b.r11.text: If one `create_promise` fails twice, keep the promises that were recorded and call `add_note` with reason `service_error` for the failed product.

b.p3.text: The outcome table of Brief A applies. With no promise recorded: if every product is noted `paid`, close as `paid`. Otherwise close as `no_promise` with the reason of the first product, in `get_account` order, whose note is not `paid`. With several products, `promise` wins whenever at least one promise was recorded, except rule 10 above.
